safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 4.0 to 1.9 days

narrative: Material PL1__MCD7ED62 exhibits intermittent demand with a CV of 1.05 and only 57% active days, indicating a compound zero-inflated consumption pattern. Lead times are very short (mean 0.60 days) but highly unstable (CV 1.29), making lead-time variability the dominant driver of safety stock. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: the large EOQ-optimal order quantity (3,195 units) drastically reduces ordering frequency and total cost by 83%, while the upward-revised safety stock of 262 units ensures 95% service level coverage against demand and lead-time uncertainty.
warnings: Lead time CV = 1.29 classified as UNSTABLE; safety stock elevated accordingly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Given intermittent demand with high CV and short but unstable lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) model is most appropriate. It allows immediate response when stock drops to the reorder point, avoiding the excess inventory that periodic review would accumulate during zero-demand periods.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (3,574 units) constrains the order quantity to 3,195 units (safety stock 262 + OQ 3,195 = 3,457 ≤ 3,574). The capacity constraint is non-binding at the margin, so no service degradation is expected.
